items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, as lever 3 of BL-823); Claude (split out on closing that umbrella)
items.title: A polity can act on ground it cannot hear from, because there is no communication rung
items.design:
SPLIT OUT OF BL-823 (anti-hegemon levers) ON 2026-09-11, when that umbrella closed. It is the LAST of its six levers still unbuilt; the other five shipped under their own ids.

BEN, 2026-09-08, naming it: before a communication rung is reached, a polity cannot act on ground it cannot HEAR from -- which bounds early growth by GEOGRAPHY rather than by a cap.

IT EARNS ITS PLACE TWICE, which is why it survived the umbrella's closure. It is an anti-hegemon lever, and it is also THE SECOND RUNG OF BEN'S OWN ARC (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md: origin -> COMMUNICATION -> conquest or diplomatic union -> a stable dark age). The arc names four rungs and this is the only one with no mechanism behind it.

IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF REACH, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ITEM. BL-837's reach asks CAN I SUPPLY THIS -- a question about materials moving over terrain. Communication asks CAN I KNOW ABOUT THIS AT ALL -- a question about information, which travels differently, degrades differently, and binds EARLY history where reach binds late. If the build cannot articulate a difference that shows up in the numbers, it is duplicating reach and should be dropped rather than shipped: BL-823's own instruction was to re-read the remaining levers as SUPPORTING reach-gating and to drop any that only duplicate it. That test applies to this item first.

THE CONSTRAINT, unchanged from the umbrella: a lever is a FORCE WITH A VISIBLE CAUSE ON THE MAP, never a term inside an actor and never a penalty that scales with a polity's rank.

DESIGN IS OWED BEFORE BUILD. Open: what the rung IS (a capacity band? a work? a property of the network?); whether it gates the scorer's candidate list or the verb's execution; and how it differs measurably from reach rather than only in prose.

DONE WHEN: a polity demonstrably cannot act on ground it has no communication to; the bound shows up in EARLY history where reach binds late; and the difference from reach is visible in the sweep rather than argued for in a comment.

DESIGN SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11, elicitation): the rung is DERIVED, not a stored capacity band or a work of its own -- it comes from either (A) immediate borders, or (B) good relations with a neighbour who shares border detail. It gates the SCORER'S CANDIDATE LIST, not verb execution -- ground beyond the rung never becomes a candidate the scorer considers, rather than being considered and then refused at execution. Design is now settled; this item may be promoted to REFINED.md.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Print the closure contract's seven readings from history_sweep, at 1200 CE
items.design:
THE CONTRACT IS A STRUCT PLUS A SCOREBOARD, AND THIS IS THE SCOREBOARD. pass_one_output_valid checks internal consistency -- shares sum to 1000, holdings name living polities, grudges name polities in range. It cannot check SHAPE, and shape is the whole of what the closure requires.

WHY IT EXISTS, stated as plainly as the handoff stated it: four items delivered on 2026-09-11 (BL-887 reach chains, BL-839 turbulence lean, BL-838 fear-of-next, BL-905 reach gate) were each measured honestly and NONE could be JUDGED, because nothing downstream asked for anything specific. A mechanism inside the Empire phase is judged by whether it moves a reading here. Without this surface, sprint 38's pattern repeats by default.

THE SEVEN READINGS are CIVILISATION.md sec What the closure is judged on: explorer set, strength spread, contact, directed wants, markets, inherited network, grudges still biting. Each is read OVER A SEED SPREAD and never per-world.

NO TARGET NUMBERS ARE SET IN THIS ITEM. The spread is measured first and the admissible band is argued from the measurement, exactly as sprint 38's done_when requires and as the opposition-bar question in CIVILISATION.md sec Open questions already insists. A number picked to make one seed look right is the failure mode this item exists to prevent, not a shortcut it may take.

A SEED THAT REFUSES A READING IS LEGITIMATE; A SPREAD THAT REFUSES ONE IS NOT. Assert on the spread. A per-world assertion here would re-introduce the forced outcome the whole phase is designed against.

DEPENDS on BL-906 (empire span to 1200) for the readings to mean anything, and reports partial readings honestly for the fields BL-908/909/910/911/912 have not yet supplied -- a missing field prints as MISSING, never as zero.

DONE WHEN: history_sweep prints all seven readings with the year they were taken; a field whose source is unbuilt says so; and the spread reading for each is recorded in the item's resolution as the baseline every later mechanism is judged against.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A directed want table: A knows B holds what A lacks
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11): a good you know exists, that you do not have, is a MOTIVE on its own. The want needs no price and this phase still has no market during its span. CIVILISATION.md sec The directed want owns the design.

DIRECTED, NOT A SCARCITY LIST (Ben's explicit choice over the per-polity alternative). A scarcity list says a realm is short of something and names no object for the shortage. The directed form is what makes the exploration age's first act explicable -- THIS realm sailed to THAT one, for THAT -- rather than a roll over a list of absences.

TWO INPUTS. (1) Endowment: what B's ground holds that A's reachable ground does not, off the four region windows (farm/ore/energy/port). (2) What B's MARKET SHOWS (Ben, 2026-09-11) -- the conditions a neighbour's market makes visible, which is the signal a trading age actually acts on. The second input is why BL-910 exists and is why this item requires it.

A WANT REQUIRES CONTACT. The table is defined only over pairs BL-908's record already joins. Without that gate it is omniscience with extra steps, and the exploration age has nothing to discover because every realm already wants everything.

NO PRICE, NO ORDER BOOK, NO DEMAND CURVE. CIVILISATION.md sec Materials are spent when something happens is unchanged. Population demand is the economy pass's and must not leak backwards into a phase with no price -- the want is a KNOWN ABSENCE plus a KNOWN HOLDER, nothing more.

THE MECHANISM TRANSFERS, THE PROPER NOUN DOES NOT. The historical analogy Ben raised is a mechanism reference only (io-standing-rules sec Terms & docs): no Earth name appears in generated content.

DONE WHEN: the want table crosses in pass_one_output, is non-empty on a spread, points ACROSS contact rather than within it, and every entry names both the holder and the thing wanted.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Wire the Empire tree into the sim: the sim reads nodes, and the rim is the explorer threshold
items.design:
THE LARGEST OUTSTANDING PIECE OF GENERATION WORK, AND THE ONE THAT MAKES BEN'S SECOND ASPECT REAL. Three trees are authored and lint-green -- 143 nodes across colonisation_tree.json, empire_tree.json and industry_tree.json -- and NOTHING IN src/ READS ANY OF THEM. (src/world/tech_tree.* is the unrelated CAMPAIGN tree loaded from scripts/tech_tree.lua; do not confuse them.) trees/TREES.md states 'the sim reads nodes, not bands' (Ben, 2026-09-10) and the code reads bands only. This item closes that for the EMPIRE tree; colonisation and industry are out of scope.

SCOPE IS WIRE ONLY -- NO GENERATION RENDER (Ben, 2026-09-11, form + notes): 'the tech tree will be available via the tech ledger later - we don't need to render it in generation, and we don't have a reference to view each polity's tree regardless.' Wiring the tree into the sim and showing it to a player are separate decisions and only the first is taken.

WHY A BAND CANNOT DO THIS JOB. A band is a ladder everyone climbs in the same order, so difference under it is only ever HOW FAR, never WHICH WAY. The closure contract's explorer set is a THRESHOLD CROSSED (Ben, 2026-09-11): a per-polity boolean read off EM-SP-4m, 'The Enforceable Promise', whose sole effect opens the industry tree and whose requires are EM-PE-4a and EM-RD-4b. That is a fact about what a realm BUILT, and no scalar expresses it.

THE FORK IS WHAT MAKES DIFFERENCE INDEPENDENT OF ECONOMIC MIGHT, and it is the half most likely to be dropped as an optimisation. A closed fork side goes dark permanently, so two wealthy realms can end the phase incapable of the same things because they CHOSE differently. Without the fork, technological difference collapses into a restatement of size -- which is the one thing this output must not be. The empire tree carries 1 fork; it is load-bearing.

STATE, per trees/TREES.md sec State: one 64-bit mask per tree plus one accumulated-progress integer for the node being invested in. Research is a FLOW derived from the labour split (a fraction of the industry slice, scaled by spire ring and contact degree), never a resource -- BL-867 (materials spent on action) already splits labour three ways, so the input exists.

WITHIN THE EXISTING GRANT, and this is asserted rather than assumed. Choosing a node is an argument to the Invest verb the register already covers (ai/AI_OPPONENT.md sec 11); it issues no new verb and plans nothing. If the implementation finds itself wanting a verb the register does not name, STOP and raise a new grant -- NR-517 is the precedent for why reading an existing grant as covering a new subject is the exact failure this rule exists to prevent.

DETERMINISM. Node choice is a seeded, scored argmax over a TOTAL order with an explicit tie-break, in fixed node-id order. No float in the decision path; the sim is integer fixed-point.

SUGGESTED SLICING, since this is difficulty 6: (a) tree state + load the store into a Lua-free TU; (b) the Invest verb spends progress on a node instead of a band; (c) the scorer, per TREES.md sec The scorer; (d) the rim reading into pass_one_output. Slice (d) is what BL-907 needs and can land before (c) is good.

DONE WHEN: a polity's empire-tree mask is real state, Invest buys nodes, the rim milestone is readable per polity at 1200 CE and crosses in pass_one_output, world_determinism is unchanged, and the sweep shows SOME surviving realms holding the rim and not all.
